field.label: Enabled
field.help: Disable to keep this rule without applying it.

field.label: Description
field.help: Optional label shown in the policy list.

field.label: Listener
field.help: Which listener this rule applies to -- a query only matches this rule if it arrived on this listener.

field.label: Match type
field.help: cidr for VLAN/network-based routing (the primary use case), domain for split-horizon delegation such as *.in-addr.arpa or an internal zone, mac for per-device rules.

field.label: Match value
field.help: e.g. 192.168.3.0/24, internal, 168.192.in-addr.arpa, or aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff, depending on the match type above. For a cidr rule, this is filled in automatically from the selected listener's own interface, and refills every time you change the listener -- overwrite it freely for a narrower range or a non-standard setup. For a domain rule, matches are exact -- example.com does not also match foo.example.com; add a separate *.example.com rule to cover subdomains.

field.label: Upstream profile
field.help: Matching queries are routed to this upstream profile. Select the local-zone resolver upstream here for *.in-addr.arpa / internal delegation rules.

field.label: Fallback upstream (optional)
field.help: Optional. If set, ctrld tries the upstream above first and only falls back to this one on timeout or a SERVFAIL response -- not on every query. Leave blank to have no fallback (a failed upstream simply fails the query, as today). Useful for a listener that should keep answering if its primary upstream is briefly unreachable.
